act0_scene1.text: At BITS Pilani Hyderabad Campus, over six thousand students, faculty, and administrative staff rely on complex digital infrastructure every single day for academic, research, and residential operations.

act0_scene2.text: When core fiber lines are damaged or central authentication clusters halt during midsem examinations, campuses experience catastrophic operational paralysis and cascading system downtime.

act0_scene3.text: Traditional campus helpdesks fail under storm conditions, lacking deterministic state machines, automated correlation engines, and verifiable cryptographic audit trails.

act0_scene4.text: Welcome to Incident-Zero: a military-grade, reactive IT service management platform engineered from the ground up for zero cascading downtime and absolute institutional resilience.

act1_scene1.text: Incident-Zero was conceived, designed, and implemented by Group 76 under the Object-Oriented Programming curriculum at BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus.

act1_scene2.text: Srijan Shukla architected the pure domain core, the eleven-state deterministic finite state machine, and the tamper-evident cryptographic audit ledger.

act1_scene3.text: Suhani Agarwal spearheaded the precision dual-clock SLA chronometer engine, business calendar arithmetic, and multi-tier escalation policies.

act1_scene4.text: Kartikey Negi engineered the campus service dependency directed acyclic graph, Tarjan cycle validation, and major incident storm correlation.

act1_scene5.text: Hairsh Kumar crafted the full-stack responsive interface, interactive Three.js hardware telemetry, and enterprise REST controller adapters.

act1_scene6.text: Our platform adheres strictly to Ports and Adapters, or Hexagonal Architecture, isolating pure business entities completely from frameworks, persistence, and external drivers.

act1_scene7.text: Eleven discrete domain modules are governed by Spring Modulith, running atop high-throughput Java 22 virtual threads and cloud-native PostgreSQL.

act1_scene8.text: The frontend combines modern React 19 and Tailwind CSS with a distinctive 16-bit pixel-arcade design language, making operational monitoring engaging and intuitive.

act1_scene9.text: Bi-directional Server-Sent Events stream live status updates across all connected stations, ensuring that student reports and technician actions remain synchronized with zero polling.

act2_scene1.text: To guarantee long-term maintainability, the codebase enforces nine automated ArchUnit architectural rules that run on every compilation pass.

act2_scene2.text: Architecture Rule R1 establishes that domain classes contain zero imports of Spring, JPA, Hibernate, or Jackson, preserving pure Java semantics.

act2_scene3.text: Rule R5 strictly prohibits non-deterministic calls to Instant now and UUID randomUUID inside domain and application services, mandating mockable clock and identity ports.

act2_scene4.text: Rule R3 dictates that transactional audit and SLA listeners must execute synchronously with mandatory propagation, guaranteeing zero-orphan ledger entries.

act2_scene5.text: Every continuous integration run verifies all nine rules in under three seconds, catching architectural drift before any pull request can be merged.

act2_scene6.text: A rigorous domain exception hierarchy maps fifteen strongly typed campus errors to standard RFC-7807 problem details with human-readable diagnostic remedies.

act2_scene7.text: Codes range from ITSM-4001 for illegal state machine transitions up to ITSM-5090 for optimistic concurrency locking conflicts.

act2_scene8.text: Global exception translation ensures that sensitive backend stack traces and credentials never leak to client browsers or terminal logs.

act2_scene9.text: These strict invariants ensure that our domain model remains rock-solid, fully testable without database containers, and compiler-verified across half a million test vectors.

act2_scene10.text: Spring Modulith continuously validates that package boundaries between incident, sla, audit, and assignment remain strictly unidirectional.

act3_scene1.text: We now demonstrate Core Workflow 1, following an incident through all eleven finite states from initial report to cryptographic sealing.

act3_scene2.text: Student Aarav Sharma logs into the self-service portal to report a critical failure on the SWD Mess and Fee Payment Gateway.

act3_scene3.text: The student specifies high impact and high urgency. Our automated Priority Engine evaluates the campus calendar and notes an active fee payment window.

act3_scene4.text: Because the service carries the FEE_DEADLINE calendar tag, the priority calculation automatically bumps the ticket to P1 Critical.

act3_scene5.text: A full priority explanation JSON array is embedded into the ticket, explaining the exact formula, calendar modifiers, and institutional rules applied.

act3_scene6.text: The ticket is routed via the Least-Loaded Strategy to Senior Technician Vikram Rao, moving state to ASSIGNED and starting the response clock.

act3_scene7.text: Vikram clicks Acknowledge in the workbench. The initial response clock stops in two minutes, well under the five-minute P1 threshold.

act3_scene8.text: Remediating the payment gateway, Vikram applies a database pool restart and enters detailed resolution notes exceeding the mandatory twenty-character validation.

act3_scene9.text: The incident enters RESOLVED. Aarav receives a real-time notification, tests payment access, and confirms resolution with a five-star rating.

act3_scene10.text: Finally, the IT Administrator archives the verified ticket into CLOSED status, immutably sealing its resolution record in the audit ledger.

act4_scene1.text: In enterprise operations, Service Level Agreements are legally binding commitments. Incident-Zero implements a dual-clock chronometer system.

act4_scene2.text: Across four service tiers and four priority levels, sixteen distinct SLA policies govern response targets from five minutes to resolution targets of three days.

act4_scene3.text: Tier zero and tier one services run on continuous twenty-four-seven clocks, while peripheral services operate under standard business hours.

act4_scene4.text: Our dynamic chronometer evaluates time consumption, firing visual warnings at fifty percent, seventy-five percent, and ninety percent intervals.

act4_scene5.text: If a resolution target lapses, the ticket marks a sticky breach. Once breached, the status remains permanently attached to the ticket history.

act4_scene6.text: Breaching ninety percent automatically triggers the multi-tier Escalation Ladder, notifying team leads, IT managers, and system administrators.

act4_scene7.text: When a ticket transitions to PENDING_USER for student feedback, the resolution clock cleanly suspends and resumes upon user reply.

act4_scene8.text: A monotonic clock generation counter ensures that whenever an SLA timer pauses or updates, legacy in-flight async timer events are safely invalidated.

act4_scene9.text: Business hours arithmetic automatically excludes official BITS holidays like Gandhi Jayanti, Dussehra, and Diwali from timer countdowns.

act4_scene10.text: Comprehensive unit tests prove that clock pauses, resumptions, and holiday skips maintain microsecond accuracy across month-long windows.

act5_scene1.text: Campus IT services do not operate in a vacuum. Core infrastructure failures produce massive, compounding blast radiuses.

act5_scene2.text: Incident-Zero models all nineteen campus services across twenty-six hard and soft dependency edges as a directed acyclic graph.

act5_scene3.text: Tarjan's strongly connected components algorithm executes during graph updates, rejecting any accidental circular dependencies at runtime.

act5_scene4.text: When Data Center cooling fails, core switches overheat, and Central LDAP goes down, hundreds of student login tickets flood the portal.

act5_scene5.text: Our Storm Detection Engine activates, tracking ticket velocity over five-minute sliding windows against the dependency topology.

act5_scene6.text: The system automatically pinpoints Central LDAP as the root cause, declaring a Major Incident and linking forty-five tickets as child duplicates.

act5_scene7.text: Chief Administrator Suresh Deshmukh is appointed Incident Commander, locking triage roles and broadcasting campus-wide alerts.

act5_scene8.text: The interactive 3D blast radius visualizer highlights downstream services at risk, including Moodle LMS, AUGSD ERP, and hostel Wi-Fi.

act5_scene9.text: Transactional cascade listeners propagate the root resolution notes down to all child incidents, preserving audit integrity for each student.

act5_scene10.text: When the Commander resolves the root LDAP ticket, Incident-Zero automatically resolves all linked duplicate tickets and notifies affected students.

act6_scene1.text: To reduce technician load, Incident-Zero integrates fully offline, local intelligence for automated ticket deflection and dispatch.

act6_scene2.text: Incident titles and knowledge base articles are transformed into 384-dimensional dense vectors using an embedded ONNX runtime.

act6_scene3.text: PostgreSQL pgvector with Hierarchical Navigable Small World indexes enables sub-millisecond approximate nearest neighbor searches.

act6_scene4.text: When a student begins typing an issue with campus Wi-Fi, verified articles on CAS cookie resets appear instantly, deflecting redundant tickets.

act6_scene5.text: For unresolved tickets, seven pluggable Routing Strategies evaluate technician shifts, verified skill badges, and active point loads.

act6_scene6.text: Skill-based routing matches Aruba Wi-Fi and BIND DNS certifications, ensuring specialized problems land with certified engineers.

act6_scene7.text: Load tracking enforces maximum point capacities per technician, guaranteeing balanced distribution across morning and evening shifts.

act6_scene8.text: Atomic load tracking prevents race conditions under high concurrency, using database row versions to guarantee fairness.

act6_scene9.text: Automated test suites confirm zero routing race conditions even under concurrent ticket bursts from hundreds of client threads.

act7_scene1.text: Accountability requires unalterable proof. Incident-Zero guarantees non-repudiation through a cryptographically linked audit ledger.

act7_scene2.text: Every ticket change computes a SHA-256 digest over the sequence index, timestamp, actor ID, action name, payload, and the prior hash.

act7_scene3.text: The admin console displays the unbroken cryptographic hash chain for every ticket, allowing one-click verification of history.

act7_scene4.text: At the database level, an append-only trigger immediately rejects any UPDATE, DELETE, or TRUNCATE statement on audit records.

act7_scene5.text: If a malicious actor alters a single byte directly in the database, the cryptographic verification algorithm flags the chain as tampered.

act7_scene6.text: Authentication is powered by RFC-9106 Argon2id password hashing and cryptographically signed stateless JWT access tokens.

act7_scene7.text: Strict Role-Based Access Control isolates student self-service from technician queues and executive administrative governance.

act7_scene8.text: Tokens carry cryptographically verified claims, preventing privilege escalation between Employee, Technician, and Administrator roles.

act7_scene9.text: Real-time updates stream securely over Server-Sent Events using short-lived, single-use stream tickets to prevent ticket hijacking.

act8_scene1.text: A premier objective of this course project was translating classical object-oriented design principles into enterprise reality.

act8_scene2.text: The Strategy Pattern abstracts incident assignment algorithms, allowing runtime polymorphism between Round Robin and Least Loaded routing.

act8_scene3.text: The State Pattern encapsulates all eleven lifecycle states, isolating valid transitions and eliminating fragile conditional branching.

act8_scene4.text: The Observer Pattern, powered by Spring Modulith event publication, decouples SLA timers, audit logging, and email notifications.

act8_scene5.text: The Builder Pattern enforces strict entity construction invariants, calculating initial SLA deadlines and priority ratings atomically.

act8_scene6.text: The Decorator Pattern layers multi-channel notifications, wrapping base email alerts with in-app notifications and SMS broadcasts.

act8_scene7.text: The Adapter Pattern bridges domain repositories with Spring Data JPA entities, protecting domain logic from database schema changes.

act8_scene8.text: The Facade Pattern provides clean, high-level interfaces for controllers, coordinating complex multi-module transactions seamlessly.

act8_scene9.text: The Template Method Pattern governs calendar calculations, providing a rigid skeleton for holiday checks while allowing variable shift windows.

act8_scene10.text: Together, these eleven patterns exemplify SOLID principles, yielding a codebase that is deeply modular, extensible, and easy to maintain.

act9_scene1.text: Engineering excellence requires exhaustive verification. Our test harness spans unit tests, integration slices, and state machine fuzzing.

act9_scene2.text: Over five hundred and twenty thousand valid and invalid transition permutations are checked to prove zero deadlocks exist in our state model.

act9_scene3.text: Deterministic testing is powered by our automated reset script, which recreates the full campus schema and seeds forty-five tickets in 2.14 seconds.

act9_scene4.text: End-to-end integration tests execute complete multi-user workflows headlessly, verifying token passing, clock ticks, and audit hashing.

act9_scene5.text: Every custom exception, from validation constraints to database deadlock retries, is verified under heavy concurrent load.

act9_scene6.text: On the frontend, Playwright end-to-end specs ensure responsive layout rendering across 1080p desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports.

act9_scene7.text: Global exception translation ensures that sensitive backend stack traces never leak to client browsers or terminal logs.

act9_scene8.text: Our test suite delivers ninety-four percent statement coverage across all domain aggregates and critical business pathways.

act9_scene9.text: The entire verification pipeline runs completely locally, offline, and deterministically without external network dependencies.

act10_scene1.text: In summary, Incident-Zero fully achieves every technical objective and specification articulated in the BITS Pilani course brief.

act10_scene2.text: All nine technology report questions on concurrency, database integrity, architectural tradeoffs, and performance have been empirically answered.

act10_scene3.text: Our concurrency report demonstrates how optimistic database locks combined with virtual threads prevent phantom updates under peak student load.

act10_scene4.text: By uniting rigorous object-oriented design with modern reactive architecture, we transformed campus IT from a reactive bottleneck into a resilient backbone.

act10_scene5.text: On behalf of Group 76 — Srijan Shukla, Suhani Agarwal, Kartikey Negi, and Hairsh Kumar — thank you for your time and evaluation.
